q: How does the BEE star rating for office buildings work?
title: BEE star rating for office buildings
short: The BEE star rating gives an existing office building one to five stars based on its Energy Performance Index (EPI): annual kWh divided by built-up area. Fewer kWh per square metre earns more stars. The bands differ by climate zone and by how much of the building is air-conditioned.
audience: Commercial building owners and tenants in India

p: The Bureau of Energy Efficiency runs the star rating programme for existing commercial buildings: day-use offices, BPOs, shopping malls and hospitals, each with its own bands. It is voluntary and based on actual use, which makes it different from the Energy Conservation Building Code, a design code for new buildings. Check the current eligibility conditions in BEE's application guidelines before you apply.

sections.h: How the EPI is worked out
ol: Add up the building's electricity use for a full year, from twelve months of bills, plus any other energy the BEE application format asks you to report.
Take the built-up area in square metres, leaving out areas BEE excludes, such as unconditioned basement parking.
EPI = annual kWh / built-up area, in kWh per square metre per year.
Find the band for your building type, climate zone and air-conditioned share in BEE's tables to read off the star level.

sections.h: Why climate zone and air-conditioned share matter
p: A fully air-conditioned office in a warm and humid city such as Chennai or Mumbai needs more cooling than one in a moderate climate. BEE sets separate EPI bands for each climate zone, and for buildings above and below half air-conditioned area, so a building is compared with others that face similar loads.

ul: Cooling is usually the largest load: chiller and AHU efficiency, set points, and controls that shut down after hours.
Lighting: LED retrofits with occupancy and daylight sensors.
Envelope: reflective roofs, shading and glazing in the worst-facing facades.
On-site solar lowers grid units; check how the current BEE format treats it before counting it in the EPI.

example.title: Worked example: a 12,000 m2 office block (hypothetical)
lines: Built-up area: 12,000 m2, less 2,000 m2 unconditioned basement parking = 10,000 m2
Annual electricity from twelve bills: 14,00,000 kWh
EPI: 14,00,000 / 10,000 = 140 kWh per m2 per year
Scope 2: 14,00,000 x 0.710 = 9,94,000 kg CO2, about 994 t a year
A 10% cut in units: EPI 126, and 99.4 t CO2 less a year
example.note: The building and its consumption are hypothetical. Read the star level for an EPI of 140 from BEE's current table for your building type, climate zone and air-conditioned share.

senseible: Senseible reads your electricity bills (billing period, tariff category, sanctioned load and units) and applies the CEA grid factor of 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, so the year's kWh and Scope 2 are ready for the EPI. It does not calculate the EPI, apply for or award a BEE star rating.
